definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese confection made by simmering beans (typically azuki, kidney beans, or other varieties) in sugar syrup and then coating them with crystallized sugar.

examples.japanese: {甘納豆|あまなっとう}をお{茶請|ちゃう}けにする。
examples.english: To have sweetened beans as a tea snack.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{甘納豆|あまなっとう}が{大好|だいす}きだ。
{北海道|ほっかいどう}では{赤飯|せきはん}に{甘納豆|あまなっとう}を{入|い}れる{地域|ちいき}がある。
examples.english: In Hokkaido, there are areas where sweetened beans are added to sekihan (red rice).

notes:
Composed of {甘|あま} (sweet) + {納豆|なっとう} (natto). Despite sharing the name {納豆|なっとう}, this confection has no relation to fermented soybeans. The name is thought to come from the similar appearance of the sugar-dusted beans to {納豆|なっとう}.

TYPES:
- {小豆|あずき}の{甘納豆|あまなっとう}: azuki bean version (most common)
- {金時|きんとき}{豆|まめ}の{甘納豆|あまなっとう}: kidney bean version
- {黒豆|くろまめ}の{甘納豆|あまなっとう}: black bean version

CULTURAL NOTE:
In {北海道|ほっかいどう}, {甘納豆|あまなっとう} is famously used instead of {小豆|あずき} in {赤飯|せきはん} (celebratory red rice), creating a sweeter version that surprises visitors from other regions.

RELATED WORDS:
- {和菓子|わがし}: Japanese confections — the broader category
- {納豆|なっとう}: fermented soybeans — unrelated despite the shared name
- {煮豆|にまめ}: simmered beans — a savory preparation of beans
